headline: Hegseth said the Pentagon needs $50 billion to scale autonomous weapons production as UNIDIR launched the first comprehensive evaluation of the Arms Trade Treaty, and a Wired investigation found AI models can be stripped of guardrails to assist terrorism.

points.text: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Pentagon needs $50 billion in reconciliation funding to scale autonomous and robotic weapons production.
Hegseth said a four-star-led Autonomous Warfare Command has 'always been' the end state of Project Agincourt.
UNIDIR, Conflict Armament Research and the Stimson Center, with UK support, launched the first comprehensive evaluation of progress towards the objectives of the Arms Trade Treaty.
SIPRI examined what Russia's draft federal budget for 2027-29 reveals about its military spending intentions.
War on the Rocks argued the United Kingdom's military AI ambitions need guardrails, as the new government doubles down on AI-defense partnerships.
A Wired investigation found AI models can be easily modified to strip their safety guardrails and assist terrorist and extremist activity, including providing detailed bomb-making instructions.
AI safety and regulation advocates have spent nearly $50 million this election cycle on US candidates who favor AI regulation, a new analysis found.
AI tools are increasingly aiding employees seeking to spy on their own employers, exacerbating an insider-threat risk frontier AI companies have faced for years.
